races.name: Malcolm Prescott 80th Birthday Maiden Stakes (GBB Race)

runners_data.name: Albemagic
runners_data.note: Steph Hollinshead's lightly raced three-year-old has a placed effort on similar going (2nd, 8f, Good) but holds a 0/1 win record; naturally sits closer to the pace than the redistributed rear position suggests, so don't expect a true hold-up run — Clifford Lee is likely to drift forward from early on in this tiny field.

runners_data.name: Feliz Navidad
runners_data.note: David O'Meara's yard is in fair current form (5/43 over 14 days) and David Nolan takes the ride on this prominent-racing three-year-old who has run twice on Good ground, both at 7f and 8f, without threatening the frame — the step up to a mile at Pontefract offers a new dimension but the form figures of 55 demand improvement.

runners_data.name: Asset
runners_data.note: Sir Mark Prescott's consistent front-runner has placed in three of his last four starts on comparable ground and will control this race from the off under the experienced Luke Morris; the yard's precision targeting of races is well documented, and Asset dropping back to a mile after two 10f runs looks deliberate — the tactical position here is as strong as it gets in a three-runner maiden.

races.paceDynamic: Asset is the lone confirmed front-runner in a three-horse field and will lead from the outset under Luke Morris, setting a sustainable and uncontested pace on Good to Firm ground over a mile at Pontefract. With no other horse willing or likely to challenge for the lead, Asset will dictate terms from flag to finish, controlling tempo and denying any rival a truly fierce early gallop to aim at. Feliz Navidad is likely to slot into second from a prominent position, while Albemagic — redistributed to the rear, though not a natural hold-up type — will trail the field. This race shape strongly favours horses with the stamina and class to close from off a controlled pace, but given the small field and the absence of any genuine pressure on Asset, the front-runner's ability to conserve energy and quicken in the straight is the dominant tactical advantage here.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Asset Controls And Wins
scenarios.trigger: If Asset is allowed to bowl along unchallenged and dictates a steady, gallop-sapping tempo throughout.
scenarios.body: Asset settles into a rhythm under Luke Morris, turns the race into a test of pure class at a pace of his own choosing, and uses his position to repel challengers in the straight. Sir Mark Prescott's operation is renowned for producing horses spot-on for the target race, and Asset's consistent placing form (three placed efforts in four recent starts) suggests he handles this scenario perfectly.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Runner Swoops
scenarios.trigger: If Asset's pace is too slow to suit Feliz Navidad, who travels powerfully and challenges turning for home.
scenarios.body: Feliz Navidad, prominent throughout under David Nolan, uses his fresh legs (7 days since last run) and O'Meara yard's current form (5/43 in 14 days) to travel onto Asset's quarters and collar him in the final furlong. Two runs on Good ground suggest Feliz Navidad handles conditions, though both efforts have been modest finishing positions and he needs to find improvement.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Closers Pounce Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is genuinely fast enough to string the field out and Albemagic produces a sustained late run.
scenarios.body: Albemagic, despite being mapped to the rear as a redistributed type rather than a natural hold-up horse, would need the pace to be genuinely strong — unlikely with Asset operating unchallenged — to mow down rivals in the final stages. Lightly raced with a placed effort on similar going, Albemagic has some form to work with, but this scenario is severely discounted because it depends on a pace dynamic that simply isn't expected to materialise.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Muddling Tactical Race
scenarios.trigger: If the pace collapses into a crawl and the race becomes a sprint finish off a falsely slow tempo.
scenarios.body: With only three runners and a lone front-runner in Asset, a dawdle is possible but unlikely given Morris's forward tactics and Prescott's preference for positive riding; if it does occur, the first two home become deeply unpredictable as natural advantages are negated. Feliz Navidad's prominent style would give him a small edge in a sprint, but no runner here has been specifically prepared for a tactical test of this nature.

watchPoints.text: Asset is the sole pace-setter and if Luke Morris controls the tempo entirely, no rival has the natural running style to mount a sustained organised challenge — watch for his ability to simply coast home unchallenged.

Feliz Navidad has been raced just 7 days ago and while O'Meara's yard is in form, back-to-back runs in quick succession for a three-year-old maiden can mean fitness is strong or it can mask a horse not quite right — watch how he travels in the early stages.

Albemagic's redistribution to the rear of the field is map-mechanical rather than stylistic — Clifford Lee may choose to push forward early given the tiny field size, which could subtly change the complexion of what appears a straightforward lead scenario.
With only three runners, any non-runner or early incident would reduce this to a match, drastically simplifying the tactical picture in Asset's favour even further.

The going report confirms Good to Firm for this 1m race — Asset's form includes a placed effort on Standard (AW) ground but three turf runs on Good, suggesting conditions are well within his comfort zone.

races.name: BYD Wakefield British EBF Stallion Studs Maiden Stakes (GBB Race)

runners_data.name: Bolt Of Blue
runners_data.note: Fifth on sole start at Goodwood on good ground; Ed Dunlop's runner carries strong jockey booking in Billy Loughnane, but its true instinct is to come from the back — the crowded hold-up contingent means it will not get the gap it needs until the very late stages.|

runners_data.name: Onslaught
runners_data.note: Richard and Peter Fahey runner with two runs banked — a third at 5f and a sixth at 6f, both on good — suggesting it handles conditions but is yet to threaten; its back-of-field style is at least genuine, and Billy Garritty has course experience to call on.|

runners_data.name: Sole Ruler
runners_data.note: Paul Midgley's gelding has run twice, finishing fourth and seventh on good ground at 5f and 6f respectively; no win or place to its name and 35 days between runs may not help sharpness on what is a fast, sprint surface today.|

runners_data.name: The Mean Fiddler
runners_data.note: John and Sean Quinn debutant with no form to assess — the unknown style tag is the critical variable; if Jason Hart elects to show early, this horse could shape the entire race, and Quinn's yard has a solid 2/14 strike rate over the past fortnight.|

runners_data.name: Calef
runners_data.note: David O'Meara's consistent claimer has four runs all returning a fourth or third, all on good ground at 5f — the most experienced horse in the field on this exact trip and going combination; naturally suited to coming from off the pace but will be hunting for a gap in a bunched finale.|

runners_data.name: Naval Cop
runners_data.note: Andrew Balding's runner has a sixth and a fourth from two outings on good ground, both at sprint trips; Balding's yard is in form (13/54 in 14 days) and PJ McDonald is a strong booking, but its hold-up style is squeezed by the field makeup.|

runners_data.name: Shaqra Queen
runners_data.note: K.R. Burke debutant — the yard fires 10/34 over 14 days and Clifford Lee is an experienced handler of inexperienced horses; with no style data available this is a genuine wildcard, and Burke debutants on good-to-firm ground at sprint trips are worth monitoring early.|

races.paceDynamic: With no confirmed front-runner in this seven-runner 5f maiden, the race is likely to begin with a hesitant, jostling start as all seven runners carry hold-up or unknown profiles — creating a false-pace scenario where the field bunches and the race effectively becomes a sprint from halfway. The Mean Fiddler and Shaqra Queen are both unknown quantities on debut, and either could press forward without warning, but there is no horse with a reliable lead profile to dictate genuine fractions. This race shape strongly favours whoever has the cleanest passage and most natural speed in the closing two furlongs — a profile that rewards horses with raw tactical speed over pure closing ability. The field holds more hold-up types than the map can accommodate at the rear; Bolt Of Blue, Naval Cop, and Calef are all genuine back-of-the-field horses compressed into midfield roles, meaning the horse most likely to secure a genuinely positive position is one of the unknown debutants, The Mean Fiddler or Shaqra Queen, if either shows early speed.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Drift And Sprint Finish
scenarios.trigger: If no horse asserts early and the field coasts into a bunched sprint from the 2f pole, tactical speed and a clear run become decisive.
scenarios.body: The race drifts at a moderate tempo before exploding in the final two furlongs, rewarding the horse who finds daylight first and can sustain speed on good-to-firm ground.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Debutant Dictates Pace
scenarios.trigger: If one of the two unknown debutants breaks alertly and sets a genuine lead, controlling fractions from the front.
scenarios.body: A debutant taking the initiative on good-to-firm ground would convert this into a test of stamina-speed balance, suiting a prominent racer who can quicken off the front.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Swoops Late
scenarios.trigger: If the tempo is genuinely hot early and the field strings out, creating room for a true closer to rattle home.
scenarios.body: Despite being compressed into midfield on the map, a horse with the most natural finishing speed benefits if the pace genuinely heats up; good-to-firm ground aids a clean, fast-ground closer.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Moderate Pace Suits Grinder
scenarios.trigger: If a steady-to-moderate gallop develops and the field races in a tight group, flattening out in the final furlong.
scenarios.body: A consistent performer who doesn't need pace and handles good-to-firm well can grind rivals down in a muddling finish; Calef's repeated placed efforts on similar ground at this trip make it the candidate.

watchPoints.text: Watch Shaqra Queen and The Mean Fiddler in the first furlong — if either breaks alertly, they could manufacture a lead that transforms the entire pace shape from a drift-and-sprint into a genuine test.

Bolt Of Blue, Naval Cop and Calef are all naturally back-of-the-field horses forced into a tighter racing position — traffic trouble in a bunched field is a real risk for all three, especially at the 1f pole where Pontefract narrows.

The Mean Fiddler's debut for John and Sean Quinn carries the highest uncertainty in the race — an unknown temperament and style on a fast surface means it could influence the pace wildly in either direction.

Good-to-firm ground (confirmed for the 3:00 race) puts a premium on early foot and clean air; horses who need to be produced with a late run face a genuine surface test at Pontefract's sharp 5f where the run-in is short.

Calef's consistent placed record across four runs on identical conditions (good, 5f) is the most reliable going and trip profile in the field — note whether it gets a clear passage in the final furlong.

races.name: William Hill Pomfret Stakes (Listed Race)

runners_data.name: Cerulean Bay
runners_data.note: David O'Meara's five-year-old has solid recent course-and-distance form (placed twice over this trip in good going) and David Nolan knows the horse well, though he is a naturally prominent racer who may find this tighter for position than usual given the competition for close-up berths in this field; the style discount is real.

runners_data.name: Holloway Boy
runners_data.note: K.R. Burke's six-year-old has strong front-running credentials and an excellent record forcing the pace over this trip on good ground, making him the key pace influence; his 0 wins from 9 prominent runs in similar conditions flags he finds it hard to hold on once headed, so the key is whether the tempo suits him to the line.

runners_data.name: Point Lynas
runners_data.note: Edward Bethell's seven-year-old returns after a 73-day break wearing a hood, has placed twice at this course and trip, and Callum Rodriguez provides strong local book — the absence is the main query, though the horse's two wins in similar going over this distance suggest conditions are squarely in his favour.

runners_data.name: Crystal Flyer
runners_data.note: Ben Haslam's hold-up specialist comes into this off the back of a sharp drop in trip and has strayed out to 12-13 furlongs recently, raising distance-suitability questions; Andrew Mullen takes over in the saddle and the horse will need a true pace collapse to get into this race from the rear.

runners_data.name: Model Yuko
runners_data.note: Roger Varian's four-year-old is a genuine hold-up horse, though redistribution has placed it in the midfield map position — it will likely race from further back than shown; limited turf-going exposure (2/6 on similar ground) is a genuine concern, and dropping from 10f to 1m on this evidence needs to be taken on trust.

runners_data.name: Mostar Dreams
runners_data.note: Adrian Keatley's five-year-old has winning form at this trip on good ground and Oisin McSweeney takes the mount; races as a hold-up horse and his best efforts have come when getting a clear run late, making him dependent on a strong early pace to deliver his challenge from off the bridle in the straight.

races.paceDynamic: Holloway Boy is the lone confirmed front-runner here and, with no genuine rival looking to dispute his lead, he should be able to roll along at a sustainable gallop through Pontefract's undulating mile without being seriously pressured early. Cerulean Bay and Point Lynas are both prominent types who will look to sit close to the pace, but with three horses occupying that territory for limited real estate behind Holloway Boy, a degree of shuffling and competition for position is likely in the opening quarter-mile. The field holds more prominent types than can all realistically secure their preferred slots — Cerulean Bay and Point Lynas are the ones most likely to actually establish close-up positions, while Model Yuko, a genuine hold-up horse, has been mapped forward due to redistribution and is unlikely to race prominently. On Good to Firm ground over an honest-gallop mile with an uncontested front-runner controlling tempo, this race shape most strongly favours horses that can travel prominently and sustain their effort through the final quarter — front-to-midfield runners travelling within themselves are best placed to capitalise.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Holloway Boy Controls Wire
scenarios.trigger: If Holloway Boy bowls along unchallenged and the pace is honest but not excessive, suiting those racing prominently.
scenarios.body: Holloway Boy dictates a metronomic tempo and the field strings out, meaning those closest to him get first run at the two-furlong pole; prominent horses who have been travelling easily pick up the momentum without needing to switch off.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Pair Grind It Out
scenarios.trigger: If Cerulean Bay and Point Lynas push up hard to sit on Holloway Boy's quarters and the pace lifts, creating a gruelling finish for closers.
scenarios.body: The front three race in a tight cluster with little respite, the pace honest enough to stretch the field and reward those who have been breathing easily just off the lead; the runner who stays on most resolutely through the final furlong prevails.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Late Closers Swoop
scenarios.trigger: If the early pace is overly strong and the principals burn each other out, leaving a gap for hold-up horses to close.
scenarios.body: Crystal Flyer and Mostar Dreams, tracking from the rear, get a clear run at the fading leaders approaching the final furlong; on Good to Firm ground the surface is quick enough to allow sustained late momentum.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Messy Race, Crowded Finish
scenarios.trigger: If the redistribution of prominent types causes a scrappy early battle for position and the pace collapses into the straight.
scenarios.body: A falsely-run race compresses the field, creating a sprint finish where race-reading and a good draw become decisive; horses who find a clear path soonest from a compact bunch get the advantage.

watchPoints.text: Watch whether Cerulean Bay and Point Lynas both push hard for the position behind Holloway Boy early — if they do, the opening two furlongs could be faster than the lone front-runner makes it appear, materially changing the pace shape of the race.

Holloway Boy's record of 0 wins from 9 prominent runs in similar going is a red flag — if anything tracks him and he is headed before the distance, he has a tendency to find little and could capitulate quickly, dragging others into contention.

Point Lynas returns from 73 days off wearing a hood for the first time in a while — watch for any signs of freshness or reluctance in the stalls that could compromise his prominent position before a stride has been run.

Model Yuko's step back from 10f to 1m on turf good-to-firm is untested in this configuration — watch in running whether Roger Varian's horse settles naturally from the rear or gets involved in an uncharacteristic prominent position due to the pace map shuffle.

Crystal Flyer's recent forays out to 12-13 furlongs suggest stamina has been the focus; watch whether Andrew Mullen holds him up and the horse finds the mile too sharp if the gallop is only moderate, which this race has the shape to be.

races.name: Pontefract And District Golf Club Ltd Handicap Stakes (GBBPlus Race)

runners_data.name: Percy's Daydream
runners_data.note: David O'Meara's four-year-old has 12 runs on similar going and four wins, has won over 10f on good ground, and is the confirmed pace-setter here; the style-fit tag is a minor caveat given it is effectively racing in its natural prominent role, and nine days since last run is a positive freshness angle.|

runners_data.name: Without Compromise
runners_data.note: Antony Brittain's five-year-old is a genuine hold-up horse whose entire recent form is on Southwell's fibresand, making the switch back to turf on good-to-firm ground a significant unknown; 128 days since last run and 0 wins from 15 on similar going are meaningful concerns, though a third-place Southwell finish showed residual ability.|

runners_data.name: Pomme Pomme
runners_data.note: Jack Channon's filly has placed on good ground over similar trips and is a natural hold-up operator who will need the pace to be strong enough to set up a late run; the apprentice claim from Rose Dawes (5) is an asset in terms of weight, and her form figure of 2 over 9f on good ground is the most encouraging recent line.|

runners_data.name: Jez Bomb
runners_data.note: Sam England's five-year-old carries cheekpieces, won over 8f on good ground nine days ago, and has the profile of a prominent racer who can press the pace without leading — well-positioned to capitalise if Percy's Daydream softens the field; the step back up to 1m2f is the key question given his best recent form has come at shorter.|

runners_data.name: Moonjid
runners_data.note: Silvestre De Sousa takes the ride on Michael Appleby's four-year-old, who is genuinely a prominent-style runner but has been pushed back to midfield on the map because the field has more pace types than the front positions can accommodate; the horse won over 10f on good ground and has placed consistently, but racing outside its natural territory tempers confidence in its ability to express that form here.|

races.paceDynamic: Percy's Daydream is the confirmed front-runner here and, with only Jez Bomb as a secondary prominent type to apply any pressure, the pace is likely to be controlled and sustainable rather than truly searching. Percy's Daydream has won over this sort of trip on good ground and should settle comfortably in front, dictating a rhythm that suits a horse with stamina rather than raw finishing speed. Moonjid is a genuine prominent racer who has been redistributed to a midfield slot on the map — this field holds more pace-minded horses than can realistically all get close to the front, and Percy's Daydream alongside Jez Bomb are best placed to secure those positions. With one horse likely to control proceedings at an honest but uncontested tempo over 1m2f on good-to-firm ground, the race shape strongly favours horses who can travel prominently or just off the pace and pick up when the leader has softened the race up — a profile that suits a relaxed prominent type or a hold-up runner with a genuine finishing effort rather than a flat-out sprint.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Percy Controls, Prominent Wins
scenarios.trigger: If Percy's Daydream leads unchallenged and sets a fair but manageable tempo throughout.
scenarios.body: Percy's Daydream dictates from the front on good-to-firm ground, and the race develops into a test of sustained galloping rather than a sprint, with the winner coming from just behind the leader; Jez Bomb, tracking close up, is ideally positioned to pick off the leader in the straight with his solid good-ground form at this trip.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Finishers Strike Late
scenarios.trigger: If Percy's Daydream goes too hard early and the pace collapses, giving hold-up horses a genuine finish.
scenarios.body: Without Compromise and Pomme Pomme, both hold-up types, would be the main beneficiaries if a genuine closing run is rewarded in the straight; Pomme Pomme has shown the ability to finish off races on good ground and over similar trips, while Without Compromise returns from a long break and must show fitness.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse, Leader Quickens Clear
scenarios.trigger: If the tempo is so slow that Percy's Daydream gets an uncontested lead and simply quickens away from a standing start.
scenarios.body: A very slow early gallop means hold-up horses are denied their running and the front-runner steals the race in the straight before rivals can organise a challenge; Percy's Daydream, proven over the course and distance on this going, would be the primary beneficiary with Jez Bomb as the most likely chaser.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Traffic Trouble, Closers Blocked
scenarios.trigger: If the race is run at a contested pace and hold-up horses meet trouble in running in a small field.
scenarios.body: With only five runners the field is compact, and if closers are switched wide or caught in tight spots they may fail to land a blow despite running their races; prominent types who are always travelling close to the action would avoid the problem, though Moonjid's redistribution from its natural position means its chance in this scenario is limited by racing out of its preferred role.

watchPoints.text: Percy's Daydream controls the pace entirely — if it gets a completely unchallenged lead, watch whether Jez Bomb has the pace to reel it in before the turn into the straight, as the race could be over before the hold-up horses get competitive.

Moonjid's redistribution to midfield means De Sousa may have to make an uncharacteristic move to find a position — watch for it being pushed wider than ideal in a small field of five, which could cost lengths on a tight track.

Without Compromise returns from 128 days off with no comparable turf form on this going — watch for any sign of rustiness in the early stages that would confirm it is not ready to fire first time back.

Pomme Pomme with apprentice Rose Dawes receives a 5lb claim — watch whether that weight advantage allows it to travel more comfortably through the race than its odds suggest, particularly if the pace is strong enough to set up a genuine late run.

Good-to-firm ground is confirmed for this race despite the official going listed as Good — watch for any horse that showed concerns on fast ground in the historic notes, as the pace on quicker turf at Pontefract over 1m2f can expose stamina limitations quickly.|

races.name: Roy Winstanley Memorial Raising Encephalitis Awareness Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Starsong
runners_data.note: The only confirmed front-runner in the field, she has solid good-ground form at 6f (3rd and 4th in her two most recent 6f handicaps on good) and gets a clear lead here; racing slightly out of role relative to her style tag but her good-ground record (2W4P from 15 similar runs) gives her every chance of lasting.|

runners_data.name: Bullington Bry
runners_data.note: Four-year-old prominent racer with strong recent form — a 2nd over 6f on good ground is her standout result — though her best is over this distance on similar going and she steps back from a poor recent run over 7f+; jockey Lewis Edmunds fits a forward-stalking role.|

runners_data.name: Rain Cap
runners_data.note: Nine-year-old veteran with consistent 6f form on good going (1W5P from 9 similar runs), wearing a visor and racing from a prominent position he is likely to secure; John David Riches' yard is quiet (0/2 in 14 days) but Rain Cap's track record at this trip keeps him relevant.|

runners_data.name: Go Victor
runners_data.note: Three-year-old hold-up runner whose form figures of 0-0-0-9-11 tell a stark story — limited impact on good ground and a clear tendency to fade in the finish; Paul Mulrennan's booking is the one positive, but the form and the race shape both work against him.|

runners_data.name: Eldeyaar
runners_data.note: Antony Brittain's seven-year-old boasts a win over 6f on good ground recently (1st in last five) and is a genuine hold-up horse whose true position at the rear is masked by redistribution to midfield on the map; 52 days off is the notable flag, and Cam Hardie will need to find a clear run from wherever he settles.|

runners_data.name: Miss Magic Dragon
runners_data.note: Three-year-old hold-up type for D Donovan, with a win over 6f on good ground in recent form and consistent placed efforts; Clifford Lee takes the ride and she carries a light 131lbs, though she'll need to be positioned closer than her natural style to benefit from what is likely to be a steady tempo.|

runners_data.name: Battenburg Belle
runners_data.note: Rebecca Menzies' three-year-old has an excellent recent profile — 1W3P from 11 good-ground starts with consecutive placed efforts over 6f — and Jason Hart's booking is a significant positive; her hold-up style suits a scenario where the pace creates a compressed finish rather than a true staying test.|

runners_data.name: Summer Rain
runners_data.note: Craig Lidster's four-year-old has no wins or placed efforts from 15 good-ground starts, and her true hold-up style is pushed into a midfield map position by the crowded rear; the form string (-05959) and style discount make her difficult to recommend in this race shape.|

runners_data.name: My Boy Jack
runners_data.note: Seven-year-old for Kevin & Lauren Frost whose strong-going form reads better over 7f than 6f (0W2P from 15 similar), and as a genuine hold-up type mapped to midfield due to redistribution, Mason Paetel's 5lb claim is a minor positive against a challenging race shape.|

runners_data.name: Coiled
runners_data.note: Mark Rimell's four-year-old has a damaging record on good ground (0W4P, 10-11-8-8 in recent good-going runs) and carries a fade-in-finish warning; Silvestre De Sousa's booking adds class to the ride but the form is deeply concerning and the style discount weighs further against him.|

runners_data.name: Power Of Chora
runners_data.note: Joey Ramsden's three-year-old holds a hold-up style pushed to midfield by redistribution, and form of 8-6-6-8-3 from good-ground 5-6f races shows only a single placed effort; Taryn Langley's 5lb claim helps the weight, but the style-fit discount (0.90) and consistent mid-pack finishes make this a tough ask.|

races.paceDynamic: Starsong is the sole confirmed front-runner in this 11-runner 6f handicap on Good to Firm ground at Pontefract, and with no genuine pace rival to pressure her, she is likely to dictate at a comfortable, measured tempo from the outset. The remainder of the field — Bullington Bry, Rain Cap, and Go Victor holding prominent or hold-up positions — will settle in behind, though Bullington Bry and Rain Cap will be keen to press forward early from their prominent styles. Critically, Power Of Chora, Eldeyaar, Summer Rain, My Boy Jack, and Coiled are all true hold-up types redistributed to midfield on the map because the rear is congested; none are likely to forge to the front, meaning the pace picture is thinner than the field size implies and Starsong's lead is likely to be uncontested and sustainable. A controlled gallop on fast ground over 6f at Pontefract — a track where early position is rewarded and the straight run-in suits those who travel well within themselves — strongly favours prominent racers and those who can track a steady pace before unleashing a finish, making front-to-mid-race travellers the primary beneficiaries of this shape.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Starsong Leads Unchallenged
scenarios.trigger: If Starsong is allowed to dictate an uncontested tempo and the field settles without a serious challenger to her lead through the first two furlongs.
scenarios.body: Starsong controls the fractions from the front on Good to Firm ground, ensuring the race is run at a pace entirely of her choosing, conserving energy for the finish; horses who track her in second or third and travel smoothly will be best positioned to pounce.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse Favours Trackers
scenarios.trigger: If Starsong's unchallenged lead produces an overly slow early pace that sets up a sprint finish from the two-furlong pole.
scenarios.body: The compressed field bunches into the straight with multiple horses landing in a position to challenge simultaneously, benefiting those who have been travelling with cover two or three lengths off the pace; Battenburg Belle's strong recent 6f form and Bullington Bry's good-going figures make them well-suited to this sprint-finish scenario.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horses Land Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is genuinely strong enough to string the field out and create a proper closing opportunity for those at the back of midfield.
scenarios.body: Eldeyaar and Miss Magic Dragon, the most credible late runners with relevant 6f good-ground form, would need a stronger pace than Starsong is likely to set alone to arrive with a winning run; both carry style-fit discounts given the congested hold-up group, reducing this scenario's probability meaningfully.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Front-Runner Fades, Chaos Finish
scenarios.trigger: If Starsong's early lead proves unsustainable and she weakens sharply inside the final furlong, triggering a scrambled finish from mid-division.
scenarios.body: Go Victor and Coiled, despite their fade-in-finish flags, would benefit only marginally from a messy final furlong; both carry significant out-of-form concerns and the redistributed hold-up horses are unlikely to be close enough to capitalise cleanly.

watchPoints.text: Starsong (front-runner) — watch whether Bullington Bry or Rain Cap attempt to challenge her early; if neither does, she dictates unchallenged and the race becomes significantly harder to peg back from behind.

Battenburg Belle — Jason Hart's booking on a horse with three consecutive placed 6f efforts on good ground makes her a live danger if she travels close enough to the pace through the first half of the race.

Eldeyaar — 52 days off the track is the critical unknown; if Antony Brittain has him wound up after the layoff, his 6f good-ground win form puts him firmly in the mix despite the redistribution caveat.

Summer Rain, My Boy Jack, Coiled, and Power Of Chora — all genuine hold-up types clustered in the rear-to-midfield group; watch whether they get shuffled even further back at the start, effectively removing them from contention in what is likely to be a steadily-run 6f.|

Go Victor — flagged as fading in the finish; if he is held up early under Paul Mulrennan rather than pushed forward, watch whether a positional switch is attempted, as his form makes a straightforward hold-up run very unlikely to succeed.|

races.name: Sarah Gusterson Memorial Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Trilby
runners_data.note: Ran just yesterday (1d since last run) which is a significant freshness concern for a 6yo wearing a hood; a hold-up operator on the sim-going figures showing 0 wins from 15 similar-ground runs, though three places suggest she stays competitive — Sam England's 2/14 barn form is ticking over.|

runners_data.name: Bell Shot
runners_data.note: Michael Appleby sends this 7yo out 8 days after its last run with a visor aboard; a genuine hold-up horse whose five most recent runs are all at 7f-8f, making this 6f trip shorter than its current comfort zone — the one win in sim-going came over further and the pace dynamic here offers limited late fuel.|

runners_data.name: Goyard
runners_data.note: David O'Meara's confirmed front-runner arrives 20 days fresh and has won at 5f on Good; the STYLE_FIT flag of 0.93 reflects that it maps as prominent rather than pure lead in this race, but with no rival willing to take it on Goyard effectively becomes the pace-setter — the lone-leader role suits the honest gallop this horse produces.|

runners_data.name: The Good Biscuit
runners_data.note: Ruth Carr's 5yo has an excellent profile for this race — five of the last five runs are at 6f on Good ground, including a win and four places, making the sim-going strike-rate of 10/15 the most relevant in the field; Jason Hart rides a horse that naturally wants to sit prominent and fire down the straight, exactly the profile this race shape rewards.|

runners_data.name: Iris Dancer
runners_data.note: Tristan Davidson's 8yo arrives with a genuine hot streak (form 612161) and has won over this course-and-distance configuration on similar ground; the redistribution note is important context — Iris Dancer is a true hold-up horse shuffled to midfield on the map because the rear is crowded, so it will likely race further back than shown, and the STYLE_FIT flag tempers confidence despite the strong recent form.|

races.paceDynamic: Goyard is the confirmed front-runner here and, with only The Good Biscuit as a genuine prominent challenger, faces no serious pressure for the lead in a five-runner field over Pontefract's 6f. Goyard can dictate a controlled, honest gallop rather than a blistering one, which on Good to Firm ground at this trip typically rewards those able to track or sit just off the pace and deliver a sustained late effort. The field contains more hold-up types than the map can accommodate — Iris Dancer is a genuine hold-up horse remapped to midfield, and Trilby and Bell Shot, also hold-up types, will be ridden from off the pace. With Goyard setting a sustainable rather than suicidal pace, this race shape most favours prominent-to-tracking horses who can respond to a clean turn-for-home at Pontefract, where the straight tests stamina and a horse travelling smoothly into the final two furlongs holds a significant edge over those needing a strong pace collapse.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Goyard Controls, Front Wins
scenarios.trigger: If Goyard leads unchallenged at a fair clip and The Good Biscuit tracks throughout.
scenarios.body: Goyard sets a measured tempo with no rival prepared to go past, meaning the lead is never relinquished at the point where Pontefract's uphill finish kicks in. Prominent horses travelling in the slipstream of a solo leader gain most, as they save energy and can quicken relative to hold-up types who find insufficient pace to aim at.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Types Pounce Late
scenarios.trigger: If Goyard or The Good Biscuit go too hard early and the pace collapses inside the final furlong.
scenarios.body: A fast early sectional causes Goyard to tie up on the rise, opening the door for horses held up who time their run to arrive late. Trilby and Bell Shot, both genuine hold-up types who have won or placed prominently in similar flat-pace scenarios on good ground, would benefit most if this uncharacteristic collapse occurs.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Midfield Mover Splits Field
scenarios.trigger: If the race is run at a genuinely strong even pace that strings the field out down the middle.
scenarios.body: A steadily strong gallop compresses the gaps between positions, allowing a horse mapping to midfield to pick up the stragglers ahead and cut down the leaders. Iris Dancer, despite being redistributed from a true hold-up role, has the raw 6f Good-ground form and the finishing habit to exploit this shape if the pace happens to suit, though the style-fit penalty means this outcome is less likely than form alone would suggest.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Tactical Chaos, Long-Priced Winner
scenarios.trigger: If there is interference or a false pace that bunches the field exiting the turn.
scenarios.body: A muddled pace that produces a sprint finish from the 2f marker would scramble the expected order and randomise the result. Bell Shot or Iris Dancer, fresher types with tactical speed, could grab a fortuitous outcome, though their trainer 14-day form and going statistics make this the least probable resolution.

watchPoints.text: Goyard's early position is critical — if The Good Biscuit challenges for the lead out of the gates, even a brief contested early pace could drain both and invite Trilby or Bell Shot to mow them down late.

Iris Dancer's redistribution means it will likely race further back than the map shows; watch whether Rowan Scott can find daylight turning for home on what is a relatively tight Pontefract bend with only five runners — traffic is low risk but position off the bend matters.

Trilby ran only yesterday and carries a hood; monitor in the parade ring for any signs of a horse that has not recovered fully, as a 1-day turnaround at this level on a firm surface is a notable stamina and recovery question for a 6yo.

Bell Shot's last five runs are all at 7f or further — the drop to 6f is the sharpest trip it has faced recently and Pontefract's uphill finish will test whether it can sustain its finishing effort at this distance, particularly if Goyard keeps it honest up front.|
